name: The Test-Case Reviewer
oneLiner: Splits a test-results spreadsheet into a passed-verified acceptance-criteria doc and a review sheet of everything needing a human ruling.
lead: Partitions a round of test results into two work-products with different follow-up. Passing rows become a clean Given/When/Then acceptance-criteria document. Failures and untested rows become a review sheet — expected vs actual, tester comment preserved — with decision tick-boxes for the lead to rule on each.
chore: After execution, someone sorts the results spreadsheet by hand: passes get written up as confirmed behavior; every failure or skip has to be summarized — expected, actual, tester note — and put in front of the scrum master to rule 'real bug or bad test?'. Across many tabs it's tedious and the write-ups come out inconsistent.
instead: The agent reads the workbook and emits two documents. One is an acceptance-criteria document built only from `PASS` rows, in Given/When/Then form with duplicates merged. The other is a review sheet listing every non-passing test — expected result, actual result, tester comment verbatim — with tick-boxes for 'Valid Bug', 'Invalid Test', or 'Needs More Info'.
whyItMatters: Every failed or skipped test gets an explicit human ruling instead of slipping through the gap between 'passed' and 'forgotten'.

howItWorks.step: Reads the results workbook tab by tab (one feature per sheet), mapping columns by header text regardless of order.
howItWorks.explain: Column resolution is by **header text, not position**, because testers reorder columns from sheet to sheet: `getRow(1).eachCell` scans the header row and records each column index into `colMap`. The expected-result rule is `h.includes('expected') && !h.includes('actual')` specifically so a combined 'Actual vs Expected' header can't hijack the expected binding. Data rows start at `r = 2` to skip the consumed header, and `colMap.status || 7` falls back to column 7 when no `status` header was found. The load-bearing decision is `rawStatus.toUpperCase() === 'PASS'`: only an exact PASS counts as passed, so FAIL, blanks, and typos all fall into `reviewTcs` — the partition errs toward demanding a human ruling rather than silently accepting a row as verified.

howItWorks.step: Converts the passing tests into a Given/When/Then acceptance-criteria doc, merging duplicates via the LLM (rule-based fallback if unavailable).
howItWorks.explain: Turns verified passes into merged acceptance criteria, with two fallbacks so it can never hard-fail. It early-returns on `passedTcs.length === 0` to skip a pointless model call, then prompts Gemini Flash at `temperature: 0.2` — deliberately near-deterministic because an AC must faithfully restate proven behavior — and explicitly instructs the model to **merge** tests that assert the same thing into one criterion. Both `!response.answer` (empty) and `!parsed` (unparseable JSON) route to `buildRuleBasedACs`, so an LLM outage degrades output quality without blocking the document. The `acId: `AC-${i + 1}`` numbering is assigned locally rather than trusting the model, guaranteeing stable, gap-free identifiers regardless of what it returns.

howItWorks.step: Converts the non-passing tests into a review sheet, keeping each tester's actual result and comment verbatim, with decision tick-boxes.
howItWorks.explain: The mirror of the AC path, but with the opposite merge policy — every non-passing test must survive as its own entry because a human still has to rule on each one, so the prompt explicitly says **do NOT merge scenarios** and **do NOT fabricate**, preserving `actualResult` and `comments` verbatim. It builds one block per `reviewTcs` entry carrying status/expected/actual/comments, calls Gemini Flash at the same low `temperature: 0.2`, and early-returns when there's nothing non-passing. As with the AC side, an empty `response.answer` or an unparseable body falls back to `buildRuleBasedReview`, so a failed model call still yields a complete, if plainer, review sheet — the failures are never dropped.

howItWorks.step: Falls back to a deterministic rule-based AC or review document whenever the LLM is unavailable or returns unparseable output.
howItWorks.explain: The no-LLM safety net — a pure field mapping so an AC document always exists, byte-identical across runs. Each passed row becomes one criterion: `precondition → given`, `userPrompt → when`, `expectedResult → then`, with `acId` numbered locally like the LLM path. The `||` defaults matter: a blank precondition falls back to `'the user is logged into the application'` and a missing `userPrompt` reuses `expectedResult` as the trigger, so a sparse row still yields a structurally valid Given/When/Then rather than empty fields. The `description` bakes in `passedTcs.length` as evidence of how many tests back the claim — deterministic phrasing, no wordsmithing, which is exactly the tradeoff when the model is unavailable.

howItWorks.step: Serializes both documents to Markdown, JSON, and — with `--word` — two docx files.
howItWorks.explain: Two separate documents are written because they have two different audiences and follow-ups — the AC doc is confirmed behavior ready to file, the review doc is a decision queue for the lead. Markdown and JSON are always emitted for both piles; the AC JSON is tagged `type: 'acceptance-criteria'` so a downstream consumer can tell the artifacts apart. Every filename carries `${ts}`, making each run a fresh dated snapshot rather than an overwrite (the agent is stateless by design). The docx pair is gated behind `if (generateWord)`, and it's specifically `buildReviewWord` that renders the decision tick-boxes — so the reviewer's ruling surface only exists in the Word output.

examples.caption: A results sheet with a mix of outcomes
examples.input: A workbook of 30 results across 3 feature tabs — 22 PASS, 5 FAIL, 3 blank.
examples.output: An acceptance-criteria document from the 22 passes, plus a review sheet of the 8 non-passing rows with expected-vs-actual detail and 'Valid Bug / Invalid Test / Needs More Info' tick-boxes.

examples.caption: A single failed test needing a ruling
examples.input: A row: scenario 'Upload a 50MB file', expected 'accepted', actual 'error: file too large', status FAIL, comment 'limit may be intentional'.
examples.output: A review entry restated as Given/When/Then, with the actual result and tester note preserved verbatim, awaiting the lead's ruling on whether the size limit is a bug or by design.

underHood.heading: Reads the results workbook
underHood.input: An xlsx file, one tab per feature.
underHood.output: Each row's columns resolved by header, and status normalized so only an exact `PASS` counts as passed.

underHood.heading: Builds acceptance criteria from the passes
underHood.whenRuns: Once per feature tab with passed tests.
underHood.input: The passed rows' scenario, precondition, action, and expected result.
underHood.output: A merged Given/When/Then acceptance-criteria document via Gemini Flash.

underHood.heading: Builds the review sheet from the rest
underHood.whenRuns: Once per feature tab with non-passed tests.
underHood.input: The failed/skipped rows' expected vs actual result and tester comments.
underHood.output: One Given/When/Then review item per test, actual result and comment preserved verbatim.

underHood.heading: Falls back without the LLM
underHood.whenRuns: Whenever the LLM call fails or returns unparseable output.
underHood.output: A deterministic, still-usable AC or review document built straight from the data, no model wordsmithing.

underHood.heading: Writes the two documents
underHood.input: The generated AC and review content for every feature.
underHood.output: Markdown and JSON always, plus two docx files — one with decision tick-boxes — with `--word`.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
A results workbook — one tab per feature, with columns for scenario, expected result, actual result, status, and comments (order can vary; columns are resolved by header text).
A Google Gemini API key for the merged, polished write-up; without it the agent degrades to a deterministic rule-based version built straight from the rows.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime for the agent.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is a TypeScript program executed under Node. One-time install per machine.
steps.firstRun: First time on a new machine only.

steps.label: Clone the code and install dependencies.
steps.why: `npm install` resolves the agent's dependencies — the ExcelJS reader, the docx writer, and the Gemini client — into `node_modules`.
steps.rerun: No-op unless the dependency set changed.

steps.label: Set the LLM key (optional).
steps.why: Read at startup. If unset, the agent still runs — it degrades to the deterministic rule-based write-up with no model wordsmithing.

steps.label: Dry-run first — inspect the workbook without spending LLM calls.
steps.why: `--dry-run` reads every tab and prints passed vs review counts per feature — confirms the columns resolved correctly before the real run.
steps.firstRun: Prints counts only — no documents written.

steps.label: Run for real; add `--word` for the docx files.
steps.why: Drop `--dry-run`. Builds two documents: an acceptance-criteria doc from the passes, and a review sheet — with tick-boxes — for everything else.
steps.firstRun: Partitions each tab into passed/non-passed, sends each pile to the LLM, and writes both documents.
steps.rerun: Recomputes fresh from the workbook's current contents — re-run after the next execution round to pick up new results.

steps.label: Open the two documents.
steps.why: The AC document is confirmed behavior, ready to file. The review document goes to the lead — each entry has tick-boxes for 'Valid Bug', 'Invalid Test', or 'Needs More Info'.

inputs.name: --excel <path>
inputs.desc: The results workbook, one tab per feature. Falls back to a standard inputs folder if omitted.

inputs.name: --word / --dry-run
inputs.desc: --word also emits the Word documents; --dry-run prints the pass/review counts and stops.

outputs.name: TC_AC_Document_<timestamp>.md / .json / .docx
outputs.desc: A Given/When/Then acceptance-criteria document from the passing tests only — duplicates merged.

outputs.name: TC_Review_Document_<timestamp>.md / .json / .docx
outputs.desc: One entry per failed/skipped test — expected vs actual, tester comments verbatim, and tick-boxes for the lead's ruling.

runbook.rerun: Stateless — each run reads the workbook's current state and rebuilds both documents from scratch. Re-run after every execution round or whenever the results sheet updates; treat the new files as the current snapshot.
runbook.integrate: Route the AC document to whoever maintains the feature's official acceptance criteria. Route the review document straight to the team lead or scrum master for a ruling — nothing should sit between 'tested' and 'decided' for long.

video.caption: A 3-4 minute screen recording: point the agent at a results workbook and watch two documents come out — one confirmed, one awaiting a ruling.
script: Open a terminal beside the results spreadsheet so viewers can see both.
Say: 'After a test round, this agent splits the results into confirmed and needs-a-decision — automatically.'
Run `node -v` to confirm Node is installed; one line on what Node is.
Run `npm install` (or note it's done); explain it grabs the helper libraries.
Show the spreadsheet — point out a PASS row and a FAIL row with a tester comment.
Run the command with `--dry-run`; show the pass/review counts it prints per feature tab.
Re-run without `--dry-run`, adding `--word`; narrate as it sends each pile to the AI.
Open the AC document; read one Given/When/Then entry that merged two duplicate tests.
Open the review document; read the failed entry with its actual result and tester comment preserved, and the three tick-boxes.
Close: 'The lead now rules on eight things instead of digging through thirty rows.'
